_comment: Hand-maintained shelf of other people's writing, shown under 'Recommended reads' on /blog.html. Newest additions first is fine; order here is the order shown.

reads.title: The Bitter Lesson
reads.author: Rich Sutton
reads.description: The biggest lesson that can be read from 70 years of AI research is that general methods that leverage computation are ultimately the most effective, and by a large margin.

reads.title: Creative Thinking
reads.author: Claude Shannon
reads.description: A lecture on the traits of creative minds, the importance of curiosity, and the techniques Claude Shannon used to solve complex problems and generate breakthrough ideas.

reads.title: You and Your Research
reads.author: Richard Hamming
reads.description: Richard Hamming's famous talk on how to do first-class research, why some scientists succeed and others fail, and how to work on the most important problems in your field.

reads.title: Be less scared of overconfidence
reads.author: Ben Kuhn
reads.description: A critique of using low-information heuristics (like market efficiency or deference to experts) in high-stakes personal decisions, arguing that underconfidence can prevent you from chasing high-upside outlier opportunities.

reads.title: How to Create Luck
reads.author: Shawn Wang (swyx)
reads.description: An exploration of the different models of luck, showing how to actively build the optimal conditions for lucky events and opportunities to seek you out.

reads.title: How to win a best paper award
reads.author: Nicholas Carlini
reads.description: An opinionated and highly practical guide on how to choose research problems with good taste, execute good technical work, and write clear, impactful papers.
